resources.string: A first-class editor surface: tabs, find and replace, a gutter, undo history and a command palette, standing on the same FileSystem backend and capability gate as the explorer.

Files are read and written through the FileSystem interface (java.io and SAF), gated as caller \"user\". This build’s editor surface is a plain text field: it backs word wrap, a line-number gutter, whitespace symbols, tab width and undo/redo itself, and honestly reports every capability that would need an engine it does not bundle.
Open a file to start editing. Files open as tabs; each tab keeps its own undo history and dirty state.
Choose a folder, then a file

Format on save needs a formatter or language server, and none is installed in this build — the toggle stays off and no formatting runs.
Syntax highlighting for %1$s needs its tree-sitter grammar, which is not bundled in this build. The file is shown as plain text.
Render spaces, tabs, and line breaks as visible symbols
Spaces and tabs are shown as symbols; line breaks are not marked in an editable field.
A minimap needs a code-editor engine that renders a scaled overview, which this build does not bundle. The toggle is disabled.
Sticky scroll needs a syntax tree to know the enclosing scope. With no tree-sitter grammar bundled there is nothing to pin, so the toggle is disabled.
In-editor completion needs a language server or a symbol index, and neither is present. Keyboard suggestions here are the system keyboard’s own, nothing more.
The FileSystem backend reads and writes UTF-8. Alternate encodings need a backend decoder that is not built, so UTF-8 is the only choice.
.editorconfig files are not parsed in this build, so indentation is governed by the tab-size and insert-tab settings above rather than by a project config.
Open binary files in read-only mode by default
This file appears to be binary. Editing is disabled
Toolbar actions define which commands are shown in the toolbar when a file is open. You can long-press and drag to change their order, or tap the button to add a new command.

Extra keys are commands and symbols shown in a panel above the keyboard. You can long-press and drag to change the order of commands, or tap the button to add a new command. You can also customize the symbols using the final option.
The toolbar-action and extra-keys sets below are the built-in defaults. Long-press reordering and adding custom commands are not implemented in this build; the sets are fixed.
Runners hand a file to the shell backend or a WebView preview. The shell path needs an installed Termux (absent — see the Shell surface) and no preview WebView is wired, so no runner is available.
Unable to connect to language server

No language server is installed or reachable, so hover, completion, diagnostics and go-to-definition have nothing to talk to. A language server is a separate program this build cannot bundle; connect one over the Endpoint book when that surface lands.

Masamune is an on-device AI harness that is also a terminal, an editor and a file explorer — a place to actually work, not just chat.
Open files as tabs, find and replace, jump to a line, undo and redo. Every save goes through the same capability gate as the rest of the app.
Where a capability needs something this build cannot bundle — a language server, a tree-sitter grammar, a real terminal — the app says so plainly instead of pretending.
